text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Drydocks council draft law to be published today. Prime Minister Alfred Sant announces changes in the council which runs state-owned Malta Drydocks -- four members to be elected by the workers, another four and the chairman to be nominated by the government. Yard's workers for past 22 years elected all members but Sant said changes were necessary to help the yard return to profitability.
- Private bus operators want liberalisation of sector to be posponed for five years, citing problems caused by drop in tourism. It is due to be liberalised on January 1, 1998.
- Opposition leader warns that local councils are losing their rights.
- The number of tourists who visited Malta between January and November 1996 dropped to 1,002,360, down 62,022 over the same period in 1995.
- Singer Debbie Scerri to represent Malta in Eurovision Song Contest to be held in Dublin on May 3, with the song "Let me fly".
- Prime Minister says government wants to help Malta Drydocks recover.
